summary: Round Island Passage Light, Lake Huron: a 1948 concrete light run from Mackinac Island, automated in 1973, sold at auction in 2014 and now privately owned.

light.characteristic: flashing red since 1959 (green from 1948 until 1959; the nomination says the 1948 green light flashed, the Bulletin says occulting)

structures.note: Concrete pier about 10 ft above the water, with a steel superstructure about 60 ft tall (NRHP); on an underwater timber crib (LighthouseFriends).

structures.material: clapboard siding with a stone chimney (NRHP)
structures.note: On the southern tip of Mackinac Island, about 0.25 mile northwest of the light. Shut down after automation in 1973 and disposed of (NRHP).

access.note: Accessible only by water and not open to the public (NRHP). Privately owned since the 2014 sale, with the tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Privately owned since the 2014 General Services Administration auction (LighthouseFriends); U.S. Coast Guard before that (NRHP, 2013)

events.note: Construction began, with a control house on Mackinac Island
Commissioned 15 April 1948; unattended from the day it began operating
Beacon changed from green to flashing red under the red-right-return rule
Day mark changed to a white tower above a red base on a white pier
Equipment operated without human intervention; the Mackinac Island control house was shut down
Control house on Mackinac Island designated excess and disposed of
RACON radar beacon installed on the tower roof
Repainted over three weeks in summer 2009
Listed on the National Register on 7 August 2013
GSA online auction closed 30 September 2014 with a high bid of $65,500

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination gives 1894 for the earlier Round Island Light on the passage's south side; LighthouseFriends says it began operating in 1896. Both are cited in the story; not reconciled.

resolved_conflicts.field: decision date for the new light
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination says the Coast Guard had decided on a permanent light by the early 1940s; LighthouseFriends dates the plan to 1936, with construction delayed by the war. Both are cited.
The 2013 nomination says the Coast Guard owned the light; LighthouseFriends reports the 2014 GSA auction and private ownership now. Both are true at different dates.
The NRHP nomination says the 1948 green light flashed; the Coast Guard Bulletin, as quoted by LighthouseFriends, says occulting green every 10 seconds. The story states both; not reconciled.
The NRHP nomination describes one diaphragm horn on a pole; the Coast Guard Bulletin, as quoted by LighthouseFriends, describes two horns. The story states both; not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Thin on people and wrecks: no keepers were named (the light was run from a Mackinac Island control house) and no storm or wreck was found tied to the light. Chronicling America searches for 'Round Island Passage' (Michigan papers, 1946-1975) returned nothing. LighthouseFriends cites Lake Carriers' Association annual reports, which were not read. The station record gives range 9.6 nmi and characteristic Fl R 5s; the NRHP nomination gives visibility of 11 miles in clear weather for the flashing red, which is not the same measure. The NRHP page numbers used in the story: commissioning and the 1947 construction p. 15; the 1959 change and the 1973 automation p. 16; the control house disposal p. 8. The current owner is not named in any source read; the story says so.
